decisions.question: package:nidana_dart_contracts/nidana_dart_contracts.dart carries the declarations of three contracts (topic-model@v1, topology-dsl@v1, topology-ir@v1). When a fixture imports it, which contracts does its node consume?

options.label: by the declarations the fixture names
options.consequence: each importer consumes only the contracts whose Boundary groups it uses; nidana.tooling.lint, whose analyze-* cases import the main library but name no IR declaration, gains no topology-ir@v1 edge

options.label: by library
options.consequence: every importer of the main library consumes all three model contracts; nidana.tooling.lint and nidana.tooling (internal) would gain topology-ir@v1, with no change to scheduling because nidana.model's first phase lands all three

decisions.chosen: by the declarations the fixture names
decisions.why: topic-model@v1's Interface says the main library carries topology-dsl@v1's and topology-ir@v1's declarations unless they name a library of their own, and every consuming contract's Boundary table assigns declaration groups, not libraries, to contracts. hsdd-config injects a consumed contract's text into a phase, so an edge that names a contract the node never uses adds noise without adding a constraint. Scheduling is identical either way, which is why this is close. The signal that would have changed my mind: hsdd-config or a checkpoint resolving consumption by imported library rather than by declaration.
evidence: hsdd/contract/fixture/nidana-checks/invocation/analyze-*/ (no CombinatorKind, FunctionRef, StageInput, TopicInput, TopologyDefinition, TransformEdge, EdgeInput or buildDefinition)

decisions.question: topology-ir@v1 into nidana.navigation: the behavior suites its gates run (navigation_conformance.dart, navigation_executor_conformance.dart through in_memory_router_test.dart and nidana_dart_navigation_test.dart) name TopologyDefinition, TransformEdge, TopicInput, StageInput, CombinatorKind, ShellClaim and analyzeTopologyGraph. Is the edge contract or hard?

options.label: contract
options.consequence: nidana.navigation starts on nidana.model's first phase for this contract, which it already waits on; the behavior its G13, G15, G16, G19 and G24 cases need arrives before it starts, through its hard edge on nidana.runtime

options.label: hard
options.consequence: nidana.navigation waits for nidana.model to finish every phase, renderers and JSON form included, which its suites never touch; inconsistent with the contract typing of topology-dsl@v1 into the same node, whose G13 cases call the same buildDefinition()

decisions.why: Root D10: hard means the consumer's tests need the producer's real behavior before the consumer can start. The model behavior these cases exercise (the analyses and definition equality) is exactly what nidana.runtime's activation checks and live graph use (bus-api@v1 G23, G24, G37), so nidana.runtime's unrestricted bus-api@v1 replay at its last producing phase cannot pass without it, and nidana.navigation already waits on the runtime shipping through its hard bus-testing@v1 edge. nidana.runtime types its own use of the same analyses contract. The signal that would have changed my mind: a navigation case that needs a model behavior the runtime's replay never exercises (the renderers or the JSON form).
evidence: hsdd/contract/fixture/bus-api/behavior/bus_api_conformance.dart (ActivationRejected with TopologyCycle, WriterConflict, ScopeViolation, SelfReference findings)

decisions.question: topology-ir@v1 into nidana.flutter: flutter_binding_conformance.dart compares bus.toGraph() claims with ShellClaim values and reads TopologyDefinition ids from bus.toGraph(); flutter_navigation_executor_test.dart binds navigation-api@v1's executor suite, which runs analyzeTopologyGraph. Is the edge contract or hard?

options.label: contract
options.consequence: no new wait: nidana.flutter already waits on nidana.model's first phase and, through hard bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1 edges, on the runtime shipping

options.label: hard
options.consequence: nidana.flutter, on the critical path, would wait for nidana.model's last phase although its cases use model value types and the analyses only

decisions.why: Same reasoning as the navigation edge. Most of what these cases check is nidana.runtime's behavior (toGraph, claims) over model value types; the one model behavior beyond value equality, analyzeTopologyGraph in the bound executor suite's G24 case, backs the runtime's own activation check (bus-api@v1 G24), which the runtime's last replay exercises before it ships. Typing it hard would put nidana.model's remaining phases on the critical path for no case that needs them. The signal that would have changed my mind: a flutter-binding@v1 case that needs the renderers or the JSON form.
evidence: hsdd/contract/fixture/flutter-binding/behavior/flutter_binding_conformance.dart (G7, G14, G17; TopologyDefinition helper at line 92)

decisions.question: Every api and shared-model fixture tree imports package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart, the replay tool nidana.model writes in its first phase. Does that import imply an edge?

options.label: no edge

Every node whose fixtures import it already consumes a model contract from nidana.model's first phase, which writes it, so the DAG already orders it.
